clue.text: Ahead of the news!

parts.note: read as the line printed at the very top of a news report, above everything else in the story

explanation.definitionFit: A headline or opening line of a story sits at the head of the news item, so it literally comes ahead of the news.

clue.text: Bloomer in a translation of Chabrier

annotationWithheld.why: Bloomer in a translation of Chabrier (3-4): CHABRIER cannot be rearranged to give TEA-ROSE and no other parse appears; the fodder looks misprinted or misread, and no source gives the correct text
annotationWithheld.clue: Bloomer in a translation of Chabrier

clue.text: Her limits appear changed in this art movement

indicators.note: the letters of the words are changed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman's boundaries seem altered within a painting school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges all fifteen letters of HER LIMITS APPEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian brotherhood of painters around Rossetti and Millais formed a nineteenth-century art movement of this name.

clue.text: In morbid lethargy, not working

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Someone lies in an unhealthy torpor and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means unemployed or inactive, without work to do.

clue.text: Record gold allowance for soldier's ornament

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a let is an allowance or permission, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A disc, some gold and an allowance make up a decoration for a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulet is the ornamental shoulder piece on a military uniform.

clue.text: Scratch a match

definitions.meaning: Old Scratch is a folk name for the Devil, whose fallen-angel name fits here
an old word for a friction match struck to light

explanation.definitionFit: Old Scratch and the fallen angel are both names for Satan, and early friction matches were sold under the same brand name.

clue.text: Lured, say sailors, in these islands

indicators.note: the pronunciation used by seamen is what is meant here

parts.note: lured is enticed, and sailors pronounce the islands' name like it

explanation.surface: Seamen tell of being tempted to some Caribbean islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors pronounce the word for the sheltered side as 'LOO-erd'. The Leeward Islands are in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward Islands are a Caribbean chain in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Blow on the wrist

definitions.meaning: the end of a sleeve that sits at the wrist

explanation.definitionFit: A light slap and the turned-back band of a shirt sleeve at the wrist share this word.

clue.text: Black boxes of Hegira chroniclers

definitions.meaning: the devices on aircraft that log data about the journey
the Hegira is Muhammad's flight from Mecca, so those who wrote it down recorded a flight

explanation.walkthrough: The Hegira was the Prophet Muhammad's flight from Mecca to Medina in 622.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft data loggers, and historians who documented the Prophet's flight from Mecca.

clue.text: Challenger's comeback?

parts.note: the Challenger was a space shuttle; its return through the atmosphere is meant, not a sports challenger

explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft's return through the atmosphere is its coming back, and a challenger returning to a contest also comes back.

clue.text: Renewal of a term-contract

parts.note: reads as renewing a fixed-term rental agreement, but the phrase means fresh vigour or revival

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a revival of energy, while literally describing the renewal of a fixed-term rental agreement.

clue.text: Love-restriction is a Scottish resort

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
a ban is a restriction or prohibition

explanation.surface: Someone claims romantic constraint is a holiday town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a seaside town and ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Start of bad seepage in Dickensian sort of house

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a leak is a slow seepage of liquid

explanation.surface: A damp problem begins in a grim old house from a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Bleak House is a novel by Charles Dickens, so the definition describes the kind of house in his title.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens titled a novel after a cheerless, desolate house, giving this adjective its Dickensian association.

clue.text: Talk about headwear

parts.note: c (circa) is the Latin abbreviation for about
a hat is a piece of headwear

explanation.surface: A conversation concerning hats and caps.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally.

clue.text: This thrust needs tip of epee-but take a breather first

indicators.note: the breather is to be taken before the tip, so it leads

parts.note: a lung is an organ that breathes

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the fencing sword is taken

explanation.surface: A fencer's attack needs the sword point, but first a pause for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts LUNG ahead of E, the tip of 'epee'. 'breather' looks like a rest, but is a lung.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust, especially in fencing.

clue.text: Piece of lamb, say?

parts.note: Lamb is the writer Charles Lamb, and a piece is a short prose composition he wrote

explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia; the capital is hidden at the start of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb is famed for short literary compositions, so one of his prose pieces fits.

clue.text: Fatigue from using axe thus freely

indicators.note: used freely, the letters are allowed to move into any order

explanation.surface: A woodcutter wears himself out by swinging the axe without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges AXETHUS into the answer; 'from using' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To fatigue someone is to tire them out completely, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ruin diet at first with bad oyster

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the word diet is wanted
a bad oyster has gone off, so its letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A bad oyster at the start of a diet would wreck it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' is the anagram signal; 'with' simply joins the two parts of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck it completely, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Consignment of soldiers in battle

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed inside the word for battle

parts.note: a fight is a battle
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers

explanation.surface: A shipment of troops sent into combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldiers' in crosswords is very often the Royal Engineers; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried as cargo, a consignment sent by transport.

clue.text: Oily kind of fuel can prove significant

parts.note: fat as an adjective means greasy or oily

indicators.note: a kind of fuel is a variant form of its letters

explanation.surface: A greasy sort of fuel can turn out to be important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind of' is the anagram signal on the fuel; 'can prove' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fateful is momentous, with far-reaching consequences.

clue.text: Go from production of Rigoletto for this verse-form

indicators.note: a new production of the opera rearranges its title's letters

explanation.surface: Verdi's opera loses its spark in a staging of a short poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GO from RIGOLETTO and rearrange the rest (RILETTO); 'production of' is the anagram signal and 'from' points to the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: A triolet is an eight-line poem with repeated lines and two rhymes.

clue.text: Some fine leg-glimpses?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, deflecting strokes that send the ball fine on the leg side behind the batsman

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fine leg is a fielding position behind the batsman, and a glance is a deflected shot sent that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief looks and deflected cricket strokes toward fine leg share this plural noun.

clue.text: Shiny finish given to work here in Derbyshire

parts.note: a gloss is a lustrous surface coat
op (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: A glossy paint is applied to the woodwork in a Derbyshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Glossop is a market town in Derbyshire, a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in the High Peak area of Derbyshire.

clue.text: Dog someday changing shape

indicators.note: the letters of the word change their form into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog will one day alter its form.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a white Siberian breed of spitz-type dog.

clue.text: Rear end of train

definitions.meaning: the hindmost part of an animal or vehicle
the long trailing part of a gown or a comet

explanation.definitionFit: The back part of something and the trailing extension of a dress or comet are both called this.

clue.text: Loopy sort of topic

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: a picot is a small decorative loop of thread

indicators.note: the word topic is sorted into another order

explanation.surface: A silly kind of subject for conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges TOPIC. 'Loopy' looks like 'crazy', but points to the small loops of a picot edging.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a tiny loop of twisted thread forming an ornamental edging on lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Stuff of a middle-distance runner

definitions.meaning: to pack tightly or fill to bursting
Steve ..., the British 1500m and mile champion of the 1980s

explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram was a British world-champion miler of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack something tight is one sense; the other is the surname of a famous British athlete.

clue.text: King born in a low joint

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
née marks a maiden name, meaning born

explanation.surface: A monarch is born in a seedy dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a low joint' sounds like a seedy bar but is a joint low on the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the leg joint below the hip, low on the body.

clue.text: Condition in which some youths are spotted

definitions.text: Condition in which some youths are spotted

parts.words: Condition in which some youths are spotted
parts.note: spotted reads as seen, but means covered in pimples, a skin complaint of adolescence

explanation.definitionFit: A skin disorder causing pimples, common among teenagers.

clue.text: Association to benefit the people of Tonga?

definitions.meaning: a mutual insurance club whose members pay in for sickness and old-age benefits
Tonga is known as the Friendly Islands, so its population is a society of that name

explanation.walkthrough: Captain Cook named Tonga the Friendly Islands; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutual benefit club for members, and a whimsical label for Tonga's population as residents of the Friendly Islands.

clue.text: Radiantly glowing like a doctor in fast time

indicators.note: a doctor is placed inside the period of fasting

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone shines like a medic during the Lenten season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'like' is a link. Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes a light that flickers softly and gleams brightly.

clue.text: Gratified that beginner can ease out crime-writer James

indicators.note: the crime writer's initials sit outside, around the other letters

parts.note: P. D. James, the English detective novelist, by her initials
L is the learner, a beginner, as on a learner driver's L-plate
ease is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is happy that a novice can push out the famous mystery writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the container signal, the initials going outside. L-plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratified and pleased both mean satisfied or made happy.
